entries.title: Introduction to Acts
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: This Book hath been held by all Christians to be Canonical; and esteemed, tho amongst the hardest, yet amongst the brightest Iewels that shine in the word of God. It is an History concerning the Church of Christ in its Infancy, and shews Gods wonderful care for it, and Powerful Providence over it: It begins where the Gospel ends, which the same Author (St. Luke) had wrote; and is of great use to prevent and confute all feigned stories concerning the Lives and Doctrine of the Holy Apostles. St. Luke having accompanied St. Paul, and having [illegible]een an eye-witness, and an ear-witness, was certainly the fittest to Record what that great Apostle did and said; and if most of this Book be taken up concerning him, it is because, (speaking of the rest of the Apostles, 1 Cor 15.10.) He laboured more than they all. In this Book there is an account of many Sermons, Preacht by the Apostles and Apostolical men, upon the most necessary parts of our holy Religion, as the Death, Resurrection, and Ascension of our blessed Saviour; of Gods mercy through him, and of the life to come, &c. and withal, how holy men lived answerably to their P[illegible]fession and hope. Who, when we read these things, seem to speak unto us, and tell us, (what they say was inscribed upon the Statue of some deified Heroe) Si feceritis sicut nos, eritis sicut nos. If ye shall do as we have done, and suffer as we have suffered, then ye shall be (Glorious and Happy) as we are.

entries.title: Acts 1:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Mar. 16.19. Luke 9.51. 1 Tim. 3.16.

e That is, the day of his Ascension. This is a Translation from the former Book (his Gospel) unto this, shewing how far he had proceeded in setting down the Doctrine of our Salvation.

Mar. 16.15. John 20.21.

f Which words may be referred, either to the commandments he gave, or the choice he made of the Apostles; both being by the Holy Ghost. The Apostles had their Doctrine from God, and were appointed to publish it by God. Especially to publish the Gospel to the whole World, Matth. 28.19. And to continue at Ierusalem till the coming of the Holy Ghost, Luke 24.49.

entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Ma[illegible]. 16.14. John 20.19. and [illegible]1.1. 1 Cor. 15.5.

g the Apostles,

h eating, drinking, speaking, walking with them, nay shewing them his very wounds, and permitting them to be touched. God suffering Thomas his infidelity to contribute to the strengthning of our Faith.

i Not continually, but upon occasion as he pleased; it was so long from his Resurrection to his Ascension: and the same place in which God shewed himself unto Moses in mount Sina. So long also he was pleased to stay with them, that he might more abundantly testifie the truth of his Humanity, and of his Resurrection.

k Either his Kingdom in Heaven, the Church Triumphant, or his Kingdom on Earth, the Church Militant. What future bliss and happiness he was going to prepare; And what means they ought to use towards the obtaining of it.

i. e.

entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Or, Eating together.

l By his order, or Conversing frequently with them, as those that Table together.

m Otherwise the Apostles would have abhor'd Ierusalem, as reaking afresh in the blood of our Lord: and there Christ chose to pour out his Spirit, that he might shew forth his glory in the same place where he suffered Ignominy. There Christ would have his Apostles to abide, that they might be nigher to Mount Olivet, from whence he was to Ascend; as also that both his Ascension, and the coming of the Holy Ghost, might more publickly be manifest; and that that Prophecy Isaiah 2.3. might be fulfilled.

n If my Father, Luke 24.49. That is, the holy Spirit promised by our Saviour in his Fathers name, Iohn 14.26. and may well be called the promise; without which all other promises would be of no value unto us.

John 14.16. and 15.26. and 16.7.

entries.title: Acts 1:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o Matth. 3.11. Water being of a purifying Nature, plentiful, and easie to come by.

[illegible]oel 3.18. Chap. 2.4. and 11.15.

p His Gifts and Graces, which were (as water on Baptized persons) largely bestowed upon them on the day of Pentecost. 1. That the Apostles and all others might be assured of the Doctrine of the Gospel. 2. That they might be enabled to fulfil their Ministry, and obey our Saviours commands left with them. It

q was but ten days after his Ascension; but our Saviour would not prefix a certain day, that they might watch every day.

entries.title: Acts 1:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r Either the 120. mentioned ver 15. or the 500. mentioned 1 Cor. 15.6. That they might more readily obtain an Answer, they joyn in the Question:

Mat. 24.3.

s Which was taken away by the Romans, and by Herod; and they expected should be restored to them by the Messiah; understanding the Prophecy Dan. 7.27. to this purpose.

entries.title: Acts 1:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Mat. 24.36.

t Our Saviour blames their curiosity about such things as are not necessary to be known; and yet tho our Saviour does not in his Answer tell them what they desired to know, he tells them what is more expedient for them to know. The petition of wicked men, nay, of Devils (as when they crave to go into the Swine) is some time granted according to their will. But the prayer of the Disciples of Christ is answered to their best advantage, (tho it does not seem to agree to the matter of their desire.)

u How long any mercy shall be deferred; when it shall be given:

x Who is, fons & origo Deitatis: to whom Christ, especially as Mediator, and in our stead, refers all things.

entries.title: Acts 1:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 2.1, 4.

Or, The power of the holy Ghost coming upon you.

y Not till then, not of their own strength, but of Gods grace, as appeared by Peter's denying, and the others leaving of our Saviour,

z and that I am indeed the promised Messiah: my Doctrine, Life, Death, Resurrection and Ascension, which ye shall testifie to all the World by your Preaching, and holy living, working miracles.

Luke 24.48. John 15.27. Chap. 2.32.

a P[illegible]aces where your testimony shall be most opposed. These words are both a command, to tell the Apostles what they ought to do, and a prediction of what they should be enabled to do.

entries.title: Acts 1:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
b Mark 16.19. Luke 24.51. As he did actually give up his life till all was fulfilled, so he did not leave the World till all was revealed by him, that was necessary for us:

c that they might be eye-witnesses, and most unexceptionable.

d Not by an external help of Angels, but by his own power, and the agility of his (now) glorious body.

e This, tho a true cloud, yet was a more than ordinarily glorious one; suitable to the Majesty of him that used it.

entries.title: Acts 1:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Christs ascent was the more leasurely, that he might delight their eyes and mind; but especially confirm their Faith the more. Behold,

g Angels in the shape of men;

h which Angels ordinarily appeared in, to shew they retained their native purity; as also to represent the joyfulness of the errand they were usually sent upon.

Mat. 28.3.

entries.title: Acts 1:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i The two Angels (in the form of men) before mentioned:

k That is, the Apostles who were of that Country.

l They are rouz'd out of their extasie they were in, at that glorious sight; to learn what was so much to their and our advantage.

Dan 7.13. Matth. 24.30. Mark 13.36. Luke 21.27. 1 Thes. 1.10. 2 Thes. 1.10. Rev. 1.7.

m 1 Visibly. 2. In a cloud. 3. By his own Power. 4. With the like Majesty. 5 With the same Soul and Body.

entries.title: Acts 1:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n Which Bethany was a part of, as scituate towards the bottom of it, remoter from Ierusalem. Hence Luke 24.50. differs not from this place; from hence the rather our Lord Ascended, that he might receive his glory, nigh the place where he began his suffering; (in the garden where he endured his agony, and was betrayed) and in the view of Ierusalem, where he had been condemned and scorn'd.

o About a mile or two, or such a space; as by Gods appointment was betwixt the Ark and the people, Iohn 3.4.

entries.title: Acts 1:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
p To the City, and to the House:

q The same probably where they had kept the Passover, and partook of the Lords Supper: howsoever for its largeness, capable to receive so many.

Mat. 10.3.

r As Elder, and first called to the Apostleship, is generally first named; and here especially his name first; and their names are repeated, to shew, that tho they fall in forsaking of Christ, they did rise again in professing of him; and that notwithstanding their Apostacy, they were continued after their recovery, in their former Office and Dignity.

entries.title: Acts 1:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 2.1.

s With great resolution, notwithstanding all opposition and contradiction they met with: Prayer and Supplications for mercies they wanted, or preventing of the evils they feared.

t Their Wives, or such women especially, as we read of Matth. 27.55, 56.

u That is, his Relations and Kinswomen, which frequently in Scripture are called Brethren.

entries.title: Acts 1:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x Betwixt our Saviours Ascension and Pentecost.

y As generally spake for, and amongst the Apostles; but now especially, to express his zeal and faithfulness to our Saviour, whom he had so lately denied; he being also designed the Minister of the Circumcision, which place he began now to execute.

z Or persons about an hundred and twenty; probably, Christ had converted many men, but these might be either men of name or quality; or mean[illegible]t of such as, ver. 21. had accompanied with Christ and his Apostles, and were design'd for the Ministry.

entries.title: Acts 1:16
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a An ordinary compellation; Speaker and Auditors were Hebrews of the Hebrews.

b viz. Psal. 41.9. must needs be fulfilled: yet God's foreknowledg and prediction, excused not Iudas his sin:

John 13.18. and 18.3.

c not onely leading them in the way when they took our Saviour, but being director of their Counsels against him. This the Apostle premises to abate the offence that the horrible fall of Iudas might have occasioned.

entries.title: Acts 1:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Luke 6.16.

d Being one of the twelve Apostles.

e [illegible], not as if Iudas was made an Apostle by lot, as Matthias afterwards; but by the Providence of God, by which every lot and casual matter is governed: and to shew that the dignity did not befall him, or any of the other Apostles, because of their descent, (from Aaron) or from nature, or from any desert whatsoever, but meerly from Gods good will and pleasure.

f Then the Apostles Office is Ministerial, and they were not Lords over Gods heritage.

entries.title: Acts 1:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
g which Iudas might have agreed for at that price; and yet the chief Priests bought (as Matth. 27.7.) by a strange providence, leading of them to that purchase; howsoever eventually he bought it, as throwing back to them their money which payed for it, Matth 27 5.

h It is said he hanged himself, which implying onely his death by sufforation; whether he dyed out of horror of his fact, or laying violent hands on himself in such circumstances as may agree with this relation, it is not material to determine.

Purchased a field;

entries.title: Acts 1:19
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i The Syriack Language then in use after the Babylonish Captivity.

k As bought with the price of Christ's blood, and sprinkled with his own blood.

entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
l viz. Psal. 69.25. What there is in general spoken by David concerning his enemies, is here applyed, particularly to Iudas, who betrayed our Saviour; whose Type David was, as Doeg was of Iudas. His

Psal. 109 8.

m Charge or Office, or Prefecture; as of a shepherd over his flock.

entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n There were to be twelve Apostles in the Christian Church, to answer unto the twelve Patriarchs, and twelve Tribes in the Iewish Church; accompanied with us in ordinary conversation.

entries.title: Acts 1:22
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
p When Christ was Baptized by him, and by that Consecration began the Ministery, and publishing of the Gospel, (which the history of his Immaculate Conception did preface to.)

Ver 9.

q All other things being consummated in that, it being the most difficult to be believed; and therefore God was pleased to attest it by so many eye-witnesses.

entries.title: Acts 1:23
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r Or Ioses, the same name called Barsabas in their common tongue; and

s (probably for his integrity) amongst the Romans, who then ruled over them.

t Some think the same with Nathaneel.

entries.title: Acts 1:24
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
1 Sam. 16.7. 1 Chro. 28.9. and 29.17. Jer. 11.20. and 17.10. Chap. 15.8. Rev. 2.23.

u The other Apo[illegible]tles being chosen by God immediately, it was necessary that he who was to act in the same Office, should be chosen after the same manner. Knowest the hearts, which is Gods Prerogative onely; all others may be, and often are mistaken by outward appearances.

entries.title: Acts 1:25
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x [illegible], Or every ones Station in the World, is ordered by the Providence of God, and their part or portion is assigned to them; and so the Apostleship was unto the Apostles.

y Hell or Destruction, not intended by Iudas, but righteously by God appointed for him, whilest he was in the World, (especially after his betraying of our Saviour) he was an Usurper in it; and as bad as the World was, it was too good for him. That these words should be understood of Matthias's succeeding into the Apostleship of Iudas as into his own place, is the less probable, because as yet he was not chosen into it.

entries.title: Acts 1:26
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
z The manner is not so certain, as necessary to be known; but the whole disposing of the lot being from the Lord, as Prov. 16. ult. they were thus as it were immediately chosen by God, and were Consecrated by Christ himself; no Apostle ordaining another, but all of them being called and ordained by Christ.

⸪ The rest of the Apostles, and the whole Church, agreeing with that Divine choice which was made.

entries.title: Acts 2:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c The Apostles themselves not expecting it.

d To prepare them to attend the more unto what they should hear and see afterwards: also to signifie the unexpected and powerful progress which the Gospel should have, it may be to cause the greater concourse to that place, it being an usual manner; and God would make this Miracle more publick

Chap. 4.31.

e To shew that the Spirit should be bestowed on them that were met there, and on all the Church throughout the World.

entries.title: Acts 2:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f To signifie the variety of Languages which the Apostles should be enabled to speak; to qualifie them to Preach the Gospel unto all Nations, and to remove the obstacle which the confusion of Tongues caus'd:

g which represented, 1. The light that the Apostles should impart. 2dly. The fervent heat and zeal which they should be endued with. 3dly. The Gospel's spreading in the World, and carrying all before it, prevailing over all errors. 4thly. The purity and holiness which they and all that Preach the Gospel ought to appear withal.

h Remained, as far as was necessary for the founding of the Christian Religion: and was not as the gift of Prophecy bestowed onely occasionally, as on Nathan, Samuel.

entries.title: Acts 2:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 1.5.

i Those gifts and Graces which proceeded from him. The Apostles having them all in a more excellent manner than formerly, and the gift of Tongues superadded.

Mark 16.17. Chap. 10.46. 1 Cor. 12.10, & 12, 30 & 13.1. and 14.2, &c.

k Than what were vernacular or natural to them.

l [illegible], signifies more than barely to speak; implying they speak each Language in its perfection, after an Excellent, Eloquent and powerful manner; as from the holy Ghost whose works are perfect, non vox hominem sonat.

entries.title: Acts 2:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Not onely constant Inhabitants, but such as had on occasion their Lodgings there partly, out of a constant respect, which both Iews and Proselytes had for that place, (for the Temple and their worship sake; it being also a place for Learning and Education, as appears by the Colledges and Synagogues mentioned, Chap. 6. ver. [illegible].) But especially now the concourse from all parts must needs have been very great; it being one of those times in which all the Males were to appear before God. To which might be added, the great expectation they had of the Messiah, made them to omit no occasion of inquiring concerning him; the Prophecies concerning the time of his coming being fulfilled, and they could not be ignorant of the many and great things concerning the true Messiah

n Whether the Iews had been dispersed in the two or three greater, or other lesser dispersions: Thus in part was fulfilled what was Prophesied, Isa. 43.5.

entries.title: Acts 2:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
[illegible]r. When [illegible] voice was [illegible].

o Either the miraculous winds was heard, or the report of what had hapned was spread abroad.

[illegible]r. Troubled [illegible] mind.

p Probably, not that the same words spoken by the Apostles, were diversifyed according to every ones understanding: for then the miracle had been wrought in their Auditors, and not in the Apostles: but that the Apostles did speak to every one in their proper and most intelligible Language; and this was the gift of Tongues, which for some time after also was continued in the Church.

w Either out of shame, that they had slain Christ, whom God thus extraordinarily glorified; or out of admiration of so extraordinary a matter.

entries.title: Acts 2:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: q Without Literature, or good Education, they being worse thought of on that account, than the ordinary sort of that Nation were; besides, they thought no Prophet was to be expected from Galilee, Iohn 1.46.

entries.title: Acts 2:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: q [illegible], signifies commonly a different way of speaking, or pronouncing in the same Language; as our Southern and Northern men differ in some words and pronunciation, tho speaking both the English Tongue. Gods works being most perfect, the Apostles might speak, not onely the same Language, which all understood, but in the same idiom and propiety of speech, which agreed to every one best.

entries.title: Acts 2:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s Descended from Elam, Gen. 10.22. thought to be the Persians.

t Between the two Rivers Tigris and Euphrates.

u The Apostles being Galileans, spake a distinct [illegible] from the rest of the Iews, till now enabled [illegible] did.

x Some particular district, at [illegible] called, as 1 Pet. 1.1. otherwise [illegible] in Asia in a larger sence.

entries.title: Acts 2:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y Who came either to Ierusalem to worship, or for any other business: It is evident, that many in or about the City of Rome, had imbraced the Iewish Religion: and of them it may be understood Iews. The other mentioned, ver. 9. were such as then dwelt in Iudea, these were such as lived elsewhere, onely now came to worship or sojourn there. These were of two sorts, The one,

z such as came over from Paganism unto the Iewish Religion, and were bound onely to observe the Precepts of Noah, and enjoy'd a liberty to buy and sell, Live, and Converse amongst the Iews: hence they were called Proselytes of the gate; the ot[illegible]er were called Proselytes of Righteousness; for these were Circumcised, and took upon them the observation of the whole Law of Moses, and had all the priviledges belonging to the people of God.

entries.title: Acts 2:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Such as belonged to the Island of Creet, now called Candia.

b The wonderful works of God; those things which God had wonderfully wrought, especially the Resurrection of our blessed Saviour from the dead, which was a most wonderful work; and the main argument whereby the World was Converted, and unto which the Apostles bare witness.

entries.title: Acts 2:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: c So ver. 7. [illegible], they were as in an extasie, (the object was too strong for the faculty) they could not fathom the cause or reason of these wonderful things; and therefore they desire one of another to be resolved concerning them.

entries.title: Acts 2:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
d Viz. The Scribes and Pharisees, and also the Inhabitants of Iury and Ierusalem; who not understanding the Languages of other Nations, might think the Apostles did but babble, and talk idlely or rudely, when they spake with other tongues.

e Or sweet wine; which done, may inebriate, and might be had at that time, tho the full Vintage was not yet.

entries.title: Acts 2:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f It speaks his extraordinary courage; after his stumbling and fall, he runs the faster, being recovered; and begins to verifie his name which our Lord had given him, shewing himself as firm and stedfast as a Rock.

g The other Apostles, probably, spake too in divers Languages; but by reason of the shortness of St Luke's intended Narrative, and it being to the same purpose, their Sermons are omitted.

h Such as came from other parts of the Country;

i such as were constant Inhabitants in that City.

entries.title: Acts 2:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Or proves that the other Apostles spake as well as Peter, and were vindicated by him:

l he mildly and solidly confutes their calumny. The

m which answers to our nine a clock in the morning, and was the ordinary time for their morning Sacrifice and Prayer, before which time they did not eat or drink any thing; nay, 'tis thought on Festival days, it was usual with them not to eat or drink, until the sixth hour, that is, noon-time: that they might be more intent upon, and that fit for the service of the day. How little soever (to our shame) such an argument would be of proof now, it was in their soberer times very conclusive.

entries.title: Acts 2:16
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: n God does ordinarily, before that he sends his judgments, and does his strange work, endeavour to reclaim them by mercies: Not onely Ioel, but Isaiah, Ieremiah, and Ezekiel, and others Prophesied before the destruction of that people and Countrey, by Nebuchadnezzar; but now before the final and total ruine, God sent greater, and more than these, and endued them with a greater measure of the Spirit; clearer and fuller light to forewarn them of, and deliver them from wrath to come.

entries.title: Acts 2:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Isa. 44 3. Ezek. 11.19. Joel 2 28. Zech. 12 10. John 7.38.

o In the time of the Messiah, called the last days frequently, 2 Tim. 3.1. Hebr. 1.2 2 Pet. 3.3. as also called the last time, 1 Pet. 1.5. 1 Iohn 2.18. Iude 18. because we are now under the last, and perfectest dispensation of the things of God; and no other is to be looked for until the consummation of all things.

Chap. 10.45.

p Before the Spirit was given in lesser measures, and comparatively but by drops; here a little, and there a little; now more largely, even to overflow.

q All sorts of men, as well Gentiles as Iews, contrary unto their proud conceit, that God dwelt in none out of the land of Israel.

r Fulfilled in Anna the Prophetess, Luke 2.36. and in the four daughters of Philip, Chap. 21.9.

s These were formerly, either representations more inward to their mind, as Esay's and Ieremiah's were: or more outward to their bodily eye, as Daniels was, Chap 5.5. and such as Peter had, Chap. 10.11.

t By dreams God sometimes manifested his will, as to Ioseph; but this is by St. Peter accommodated to the Gospel times. The Prophets spake suitably to them, unto whom they preached; and the Apostle rightly understands by these expressions, the manifold and more clear Revelation of the will of God in Christ.

entries.title: Acts 2:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: u To shew what all ought to be, that hope for to receive any benefit or comfort from the promises of God, either in the Law or Gospel, the Old or New Testament; viz. such as seek and serve God; but to the disobedient and unbelieving, there is not a comfortable word in all the Book of God. Some read without the Pronoun on servants and handmaids; to shew that God doth not despise men of the lowest rank and condition in the World, but that the promises of the Spirit is made unto them also.

entries.title: Acts 2:19
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: x As St. Peter had declared the promises unto such as would be drawn by the cords of Love: so here, on the other side, he us[illegible]th threatnings, and declares the terrors of the Lord, if so that they will be perswaded. These wonders were such as did precede the Destruction of Ierusalem, or shall forerun the Destruction of the whole World.

entries.title: Acts 2:20
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y This agrees with the other words in the fore-cited Prophecy, Ioel 2.31. How these amazing signs shall be fulfilled, whether literally, and by what means; Or whether onely, that the consternation and dread upon men shall be so great, as expecting the change of the whole frame of nature; is not so material for us to know, as it is to be always prepared for it.

z [illegible], Manifest and illustrious days; and it may be taken in a comfortable sense, and will be a comfortable day indeed, to all that prepared[illegible]y wait for it; for 'tis the day of the Lord, 'tis Christ's day, in which he will be magnified over his enemies, and in his friends, children, and servants.

entries.title: Acts 2:21
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Rom. 10.13.

a That he may prepare thus a people for the Lord; the Apostle shews by what means they and we may escape. Pray in faith unto him: The Name is that whereby any one is known; and the Lords Name is his Attributes, Goodness, Power, Wisdom, Faithfulness, &c. Prov. 18.10. The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth unto it, and is safe.

entries.title: Acts 2:22
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
b For so Pilate had called our Saviour through contempt, in his Superscriptions on the Cross, and that they might certainly know of whom he spake, and that he was not now (as formerly) ashamed to own him: he mentions our Saviour under that name here,

c demonstrated, and beyond any contradiction, proved to be the Messiah: (for this was that great truth St. Peter Preached upon, that Christ whom Pilate had condemned, and called Iesus of Nazareth, was indeed the Son of God, and the true Messiah.)

d The critical difference is not so material; It was ordinary to add many words, to shew the greatness of the matter spoken of; indeed all sorts of wonderful works Christ did, and so many, and so great, as no variety of words can express.

e Those that are not convinced, are self-condemned.

entries.title: Acts 2:23
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap 4.28.

f That the Apostle might take away the offence of the Cross of Christ, he declares unto them, that he did not suffer by chance, but by the wise and holy Providence of God, who had ordered, and by his Prophets foretold, what he should suffer before he did enter into glory, Luke 24.26. Yet this did no way excuse those who were instrumental in his death; for notwithstanding Gods determinate Counsel concerning it, he tells the Iews. The determination of God, as it does not necessitate to, so it does not excuse any from sin

Chap. 5 30.

⸫ By the Romans who were truly [illegible], without any Law of God: What the Iews urged or occasioned the Romans to do, is charged justly upon them as their Act.

entries.title: Acts 2:24
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Ver. 32. Chap. 3.15. & 4.10 & 10.40. & 13.30, 34. & 17.31. Rom. 4.24. and 8.11. 1 Cor. 6.14. and 15.15. Gal. 1.1. 1 Thes. 1.10. Heb. 13.20.

h Christ rose by his own Power as God; it being perhaps too strong meat to be given at first to such who were under so great prejudices against our Saviour: but by consequence in the following discourse, he sufficiently shews it.

i The same word [illegible], variously pointed, signifying either a cord or pain, the metaphor of loosing agrees with it.

k Tho our Lord endured now more pain, after he had said, It is fulfilled, and had yeilded up the Ghost: yet whilest he was in the grave, being under the power of death, the pains of death are said to be loosed at his Resurrection.

l Long, much less for ever; being such an one as David spake of.

entries.title: Acts 2:25
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Psal. 16.8. I foresaw the Lord always before my face. In the Psalm it is, I have set the Lord: the Apostle following the reading of the Seventy, then in use and known; and to the same sense; for by Faith we both see God, and place our confidence in him. David, and especially our Saviour, doing and enduring all things as in the sight of God, whom he knew to be both careful of him, and ready to help him. Thus in all troubles, there is no such approved comfort, as the seeing or acknowledging the Will of God conce[illegible]ning them, his Power to preserve us under them, and his promises to deliver us from them. Christ and all that are Christs, do conflict under the eye, and in the sight of God; as Souldiers whilest their General looks on.

n The place of the Advocate, for one that is accused or endangered.

entries.title: Acts 2:26
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o Because of Gods nearness to, or presence with him.

p Christs and his peoples joy is solid and true, real and inward, and may bear the rest, res severa est verum gaudium.

q In the 16. Psalm, ver. 9. 'tis my glory, as the tongue is frequently called; communicating our thoughts or apprehensions by speech, being the excellency of a reasonable Creature.

r Or my body:

s Or be in the grave, as in a Tabernacle, (ordinarily a moveable, always no durable abiding place)

t That is of the Resurrection, and going out of that Tabernacle of the grave.

entries.title: Acts 2:27
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u That is me; the Soul is put for the person, as Rom. 13.1. Let every soul be subject: and sometimes for a dead Body, as Levit. 19.28. Numb. 5.2. and in divers other places, [illegible] that signifies a Soul, is so used.

x The word [illegible], is put [illegible]ither for the grave, or for the place of the damned. Being these words are alledg'd as a proof of Christs Resurrection, and that our Saviours Soul was certainly in Paradice, where he promised to the penitent thief, that he should be with him: it seems rather to be mean'd of the grave, which according to this Prophecy, could not hold our blessed Saviours body so long, as that it should corrupt in it. If David by his Soul, here did mean our Saviour, because he was as it were the Soul of his Soul, and Life of his Life, it shews how he did, and how we ought to value him.

y As being Anointed, Sanctified, and sent by God.

entries.title: Acts 2:28
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
z God is frequently said to make these mercies known to us, which he bestows upon us: (The ways of Life) of of a true Life; which is Life indeed. David in these words celebrates Gods delivering of him from his grievous afflictions and exile: (in which he was looked upon by others, and by himself, as a dead man) yet was brought again to see the Temple, and enjoy the Ordinances of God; without which, his life was as no life unto him. So our Saviour, after his Death and Passion, arose, and Ascended into Heaven, and lives for ever to make Intercession for us.

a That is, with thy presence or manifestation of thy love and favour.

entries.title: Acts 2:29
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
b St. Peter bespeaks this attention and favour; intimating, he was one of the same Nation with themselves, than which nothing could more recommend him.

Or, I may.

1 Kin. 2.10. Chap. 13.36.

c David was had in great veneration, and his memory very precious amongst this people, as was Abrahams, Isaacs, and Iacobs; who were the chief of their Fathers:

d as in the 1 Kings 2.10. and else where is recorded of him, which they firmly believed.

d Or Monument is with us; either not wholly spoiled by the Barbarous enemies, who had destroyed Ierusalem; or rather repaired after the Captivity, to keep up the memory of so great and good a man. But by this it appeared, that David did not speak these things concerning himself, who must needs have seen corruption; (themselves being witnesses) for on that account they respected his Tomb, as being the Repository of his ashes.

entries.title: Acts 2:30
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Rom. 1.3. 2 Tim. 2.8.

e Not barely had sworn, which had been sufficient; but to shew the excellency of the matter, and the necessity of our believing of it, as also the solemnity of the words, Psal. 132.11.

f Such as should descend from him, as the Virgin Mary did.

g As to his human Nature, which our Saviour did truly partake of, being in the form of a servant.

h By the Power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of his Virgin-mother as to his Incarnation; and by the same Power out of the grave, in his Resurrection.

i As Luke 1.32, 33. Not as a Temporal King, for his Kingdom is not of this world but as David ruled over all the people of God, so does Christ, and shall do for ever.

entries.title: Acts 2:31
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k By a Prophetical eye; unto which any thing that was reveal'd, was as certain and manifest, as ought could be to the eye of the body.

l By the same Prophetical Spirit, and with the same certainty, which he spake of the Incarnation, he spake also of the Resurrection. Of the rest see ver. 27.

Psal. 16.10.

entries.title: Acts 2:32
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Ver. 24.

m Whom ye Crucified, and we Preach; (whereof we are all witnesses) they had now received the power spoken of, and promised, Chap. 1. and testifie what they had heard, and seen, and felt, and all agree in; tho they could get nothing by it, but hatred, and persecution, nay, death.

Chap. 1.8.

entries.title: Acts 2:33
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 5.31. Phil. 2.9.

n That is, by the Power of God, spoken after the manner of men; the right hand being that we commonly do any thing with: Some read at the right hand of God; and then the Apostle Preaches Christs Ascension too, and his being justified by God, tho he had been condemned by men.

John 14.26. and 15.26. Chap. 1.4.

o Psal. 68.18.

Chap. 10.45.

p In the fiery cloven tongues:

q In the divers Languages which are spoken.

entries.title: Acts 2:34
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r Hence St. Peter here proves that these words spoken by David, were not principally to be understood concerning himself, but concerning Christ the Messiah; for David as to his body, was in the Sepulchre, which on that account was kept amongst them.

1 Cor. 15.25 Eph. 1.20. Heb. 1.13.

s The Eternal Father unto his Eternal Son, who was now made flesh: hence our Saviour proves his Divinity, Matth. 22.45. The words here refer'd to, are Psal. 110.1.

entries.title: Acts 2:35
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: t Christ is Commissionated and impowred to reign over, and govern all Creatures, and all their actions, till the consummation of all things, so long as the World lasts; in which he, his people, and truths, will have enemies, Eph. 1.20, 21, 22. 1 Cor. 15.27, 28.

entries.title: Acts 2:36
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u This is the conclusion which the Apostle infers from the premises, applying what he had said very close and home; or it would not in all likelyhood have had so good an effect. Ye have Crucified, ye are the Men

x over all the Creatures, beyond what the first Adam was; and Christ King over all the people of God, to rule in them, and reign for them; for to this purpose he was the Christ, or the anointed of God, declared by God to be so, and owned for such by all that believed in him.

entries.title: Acts 2:37
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Luke 3.10. Chap 9 6. and 16.30.

y So great and true their grief, they were concerned as if they had been run thorow; (the pains the mind suffer are most acute) this was foretold, Zech 12.10.

z An ordinary compellation which the Apostle had given them, ver. 29.

a Not what we shall say or believe; Conversion, if real, goes further than Profession, and is in heart and deed, not in speech and word onely: they desire to know if that there be any hope, that such sinners as they, might obtain forgiveness of their sins.

entries.title: Acts 2:38
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 3.19.

c Not excluding the Name of the Father and the Holy Ghost; in whose name, as well as in the name of the Son, they were to Baptize, Matth. 28.19. but the name of Jesus is here mentioned, because they had not yet known, (but persecuted and slain him) whom henceforward they must profess, and that they look for pardon and Salvation onely through him.

d Thus Saul or Paul is said to wash away his sins by Baptism, Chap. 22.16. and this Apostle elsewhere says, that Baptism saves us, 1 Pet. 3.21. which he explains to be, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good Conscience, &c.

e 1. His internal gifts, confirmation, and strengthning in the faith. 2. External gifts, as that of speaking with tongues, which they heard; both, or either of these, according to their conditions or stations, God would bestow upon them.

b Which includes amendment of life, Matth. 3.7. Luke 3.8.

entries.title: Acts 2:39
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Lest they should doubt of pardon and grace, their sin having been so great; St. Peter here gives them a ground of hope, they being the descendents from Abraham, unto whom especially this was promised, Ier. 31.34.

Joel 2.2[illegible].

g That is, to the Gentiles as well as to the Iews who were said to be a people near unto God, as the Gentules were said to be afar off, Isaiah 57.19. Eph. 2.13.

h Vocation, whethe[illegible] external by the word onely, or intern[illegible]l by the Spirit also, depends on the pleasure of God; but the same promises of pardon and acceptance upon Repentance, made unto the Iews, are as effectually to be trusted unto by any of the Gentiles, as by any formerly amongst the Iews.

entries.title: Acts 2:40
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i The Sermons of the Apostles, or of our Saviour, are not all set down by the holy Writers; but onely so mu[illegible]h as God saw necessary for his Church to know and believe.

k Using Gods Name and Authority, and calling him as it were to witness.

l No less than the Salvation of our Souls, depends upon our forsaking wicked and prophane persons in their ungodly courses.

m The whole World lyes in wickedness; but especially the Scribes and Pharisees, and other such declared enemies of Christ Jesus.

entries.title: Acts 2:41
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n Some still remained in their unbelief and hardness of heart; tho never men spake as the Apostles now spake, with divers tongues, &c.

o To the Church, or the 120. formerly mentioned, Phil. 1.15. This was the effect of Christs prayer, Luke 23.34. for his persecutors; and of the promise of the Spirit now fulfilled, whereby in the day of his Power they were made willing.

entries.title: Acts 2:42
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
p Speak the reality of their Conversion, and that they were not onely for the present affected with what they had heard and seen.

Ver. 46.

q These three parts of worship were frequently, if not always in those purer times used together: tho some understand by breaking of bread, their civil fellowship and community; yet breaking being a holy rite used by our Saviour, at the institution of his Supper, Matth. 26 26. and breaking of bread being here put in conjunction with Preaching and Praying, the celebration of the Eucharist, if not onely mean d, is chiefly to be understood in this place. (Prayers) all those kind of Prayers mentioned by St. Paul. 1 Tim. 2.1. as also their frequent praying, is implyed; thus by an united force, they laboured to pull down mercies upon themselves and others, and to do violence unto the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.title: Acts 2:43
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r That is upon every man; not onely on them that were present, and perswaded to believe on Christ, whom the Apostles Preached; but on such also as were inform'd of those miraculous things which now hapned; so that by this means, the Apostles were had in great esteem and respect by the people.

Mark 16.17. Chap. 5.12.

entries.title: Acts 2:44
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s Not that they lived together in one house or street, but that they met (and that frequently) together in the holy exercises of their Religion: and that manner of some which St. Paul speaks of, Heb. 10.25. to forsake the Assembling of themselves together, was a sin not yet known in the Church.

Cha. 4.32, 34.

t This was onely at that place Ierusalem, and at that time, when the wants of some, and the charity of others, may well be presumed to be extraordinary: and there is no such thing as community of goods here required or practised. Christs Gospel does not destroy the Law; and the eighth Commandment is still in force, which it could not be, if there were no propriety, or meum and tuum now: nay, after this, the possession which Ananias sold, is adjudg'd by this Apostle to have been Ananias his own, and so was the money too which he had received for it, Chap. 5.4. And these, all things which they had in common, must either be restrained to such things as every one freely laid aside for the poor; or that it speaks the extraordinary charitable disposition of those new Converts, that they would rather have parted with any thing, nay, with their all, than that any of their poor brethren should have wanted.

entries.title: Acts 2:45
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Isa. 58.7.

u Those proportions of their estate they set apart to this charitable work; whether they did arise out of the sale of House and Land, called possessions, or of any Chattels or moveable estate called here goods; but that they did not divest themselves of all propriety, appears in that we find soon after this, Chap. 12.12. Mary the mother of St. Mark to have a house, and Lydia after she was baptized, did not renounce any propriety in her house, Chap. 16.15. but intreated St. Paul, and those who were with him, to come into her House &c.

entries.title: Acts 2:46
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x In the Court and porches of the Temple, whether the people did use to resort, at the time of the Morning and Evening Sacrifice, and Prayers; that by means of the great concourse at such times, they might have the better opportunity to Preach the Gospel amongst [illegible]hem; casting that net where they found most fish.

y Not onely Celebrating the Eucharist, but their Love-feasts which they usually had at that time, as 1 Cor. 11.21, 22.

Or, At home.

z now here, now there as they could convenienely; the Richer also entertaining their Poorer brethren at their Tables.

a If the former words be understood of the Sacrament of the Lords Supper, then these words speak the great Spiritual strength, cheer and comfort they got by it: if we understand them of the ordinary meats which they willingly bestowed one upon another, the Rich were more than recompenced with inward peace and satisfaction, for what they gave unto their poor brethren.

entries.title: Acts 2:47
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
b Acknowledging him who teacheth one to want, and another to abound:

Luke 2.5[illegible]. Chap. 4.33.[illegible] Rom. 14.18.

c that is, generally to be understood, amongst them that continued yet without the pale of the Church; the goodness, meekness, and patience of the Apostles, and the rest of the believers, did wonderfully prevail to beget a good opinion of them.

Chap 5.14.

d Salvation is (to be sure) onely from the Lord: Not Peters Sermons, no, nor the Miracles of fiery cloven tongues, and the rushing mighty winds, could have converted any, but [illegible] that which was signified there, viz. the powerful operation of the Spirit of God in their hearts.

entries.title: Acts 3:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 14.8.

d And not by any casualty, that so the miracle might be the greater, and the Power of the God of Nature appear.

e By which it was manifest, that it could not be by any correspondence betwixt the Apostles and the lame man upon this occasion.

f Where there must needs be the greater notice taken of him none going in or out, but such as might see him.

g For the excellency of the workmanship: It was at the entring into the second Court, or the Court of the Iews from that of the Gentiles. This man out of pride, being unwilling to beg of the Gentiles, tho Proselyted, (whom they did contemn) or out of policy, hoping to receive more of the Iews, whom he is nearer related to.

John. 9.[illegible]

h Poverty is no sign of Gods disfavour; (our blessed Redeemer is in an especi[illegible] manner called Caput pauperum) but lameness in this man, divers miseries, and calamities in others, bring them to the knowledge of Christ, and Salvation through him.

entries.title: Acts 3:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: i Tho lame; every one hath something that is truly valuable, and matter of praise and thanks unto God.

entries.title: Acts 3:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: k The eye affects the heart, and speaks the compassion he had of this poor man, whom he did not disdain thorowly and [illegible]eriously to behold: he excites the lame mans expectation, and requires his Attention, that he might the more mind the manner and means of his cure, and be the better prepared to give God the glory of it.

entries.title: Acts 3:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: m With his eyes and mind too; being intent upon the Apostles, this he was commanded to do, and it succeeds beyond all hopes: Thus we receive of God daily, more than we can ask or think.

entries.title: Acts 3:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o A power from Christ to heal.

p I apply it to thee, and will make it effectual for thee.

Chap 4.10.

q In the power, or at the command of Jesus Christ; and trusting unto his promised assistance, who can speak to things that are not, as if they were.

r Our Saviour was usually so called, and being known by that name, the Apostle does not decline it, tho it had been by many (without cause) given him by way of reproach.

That is, at hand or about me, neither had he much elsewhere; the Apostles abounded indeed, but in grace, not in riches.

entries.title: Acts 3:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s Not disdaining to take hold of a poor cripple [illegible] beggar; as also being fully perswaded of Christs presence with him for his cure: and

t that it might the more evidently appear, that this was the work of God, who can without means, and on a suddain, bring ought to perfection.

u Whence his lameness did proceed; thus God can say unto the weak, Be strong.

entries.title: Acts 3:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: x Thus was fulfilled that Prophecy of Isaiah, Chap. 35.6. then shall the lame man leap as an hart; and thus the lame man manifested that he was perfectly cured; tho in an instant, walking, and leaping, and praising God, to whom alone he attributed that sudden, and perfect (and therefore) Miraculous cure; nay, he attributes nothing unto the means; the Apostles words he knew did little or nothing, but God i[illegible] all in all unto him: and he to evidence the truth of the Miracle that was wrought upon him, and that his Soul rejoyced in God his Saviour.

entries.title: Acts 3:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: z This Miracle was so publickly done, that none could deny the matter of fact; which the enemies of the Gospel are forced to confess, Chap. 4.16.

entries.title: Acts 3:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a The very same lame beggar, probably, notoriously known to many: which

b being so much contrary to what they had seen but a little while before, when he had begged their alms; and as he reasoned well Iohn 9.32. Since the world began, was it not heard, that any opened the eyes of one that was born blind: So it was never heard, that any strengthened thus the feet of him that was born lame.

entries.title: Acts 3:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
b In an extasy of thankfulness unto them, they having been the instruments of so great a mercy from God towards him; as also out of fear, lest when they were gone, he might relapse: He that found so great a change in himself, could not but be as much surprized, as they that saw the change upon him.

John 10.23. Chap. 5.12.

c Not that which was built by Solomon, for that was destroyed by the Babylonians, as the rest of the Temple was, 2 Kings 25.9 unless some part of this porch might not be consumed by the fire, when the other parts of the Temple were burned: some morsel often escaping the jaws of that devouring element fire; or it may be it was built in the re-edification of the Temple, in the same place where Solomons porch had stood, and thence called by the former name that was so much renown'd. If any wonder that a porch should hold so many thousands of people, in as much as Chap 4.4. five thousand of them are said to be converted. This porch is thought, not onely to have been the Court of the Gentiles, and that of the Iews, that is, the outward and inward Court; but to have contain'd a great part of the Court of the Gentiles, if the whole Court of the Gentiles might not be so called, as being indeed but a porch, or an entrance into the Court of the Iews.

entries.title: Acts 3:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
d For he said, an ordinary Hebraism, tho no question was put unto him; thus the Evangelists tells us, that our Saviour answered and said, when there was no previous question spoken of, Matth. 11.25. Nay, Jesus answered and said unto the fig-tree, Mark 11.14. That is, he spake powerfully unto it.

e An ingratiating compellation, they ever valuing themselves and others on that account

f Holiness, were it never so real, and great in men, cannot cause the least Miracle, altho it is it self, all things considered, a very great one.

entries.title: Acts 3:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 5.30.

John 17.1.

h The Rulers, at whose command our blessed Saviour was appehended, bound, and delivered unto Pilate, Matth. 27.1, 2.

Mark 15.11. Luke 23.18. John 18.40.

i This is charged upon the common sort of people also, who were earnest in crying, Matth. 27.25. His blood be upon us, and our children. Their sin is here ripped up, and their sore searched to the quick, that they might entertain the word of Salvation with the greater attention and desire.

g He mentions them, because the promises of the Messiah was made to them. Hath glorified his Son Jesus, or his servant; for so also he is called, Isaiah 53.11. and that he might redeem us, he took upon him the form of a servant, and was obedient to the death of the Cross, and did that great work of Redemption, which God sent him into the World to do.

entries.title: Acts 3:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Christ the Anointed; when they cryed out as with one voice, Iohn 19.15. We have no king but Cesar; disclaiming our Redeemer, and his being anointed over them:

l To wit, Barabbas crying out, Iohn 18.40. Not this man, but Barabbas, which much aggravated their impiety, when the choice was given unto them of two, so vastly different, the just Jesus, and the murderous Barabbas; they chose the latter to their Destruction and Confusion unto this present day: Where will blindness of mind, and hardness of heart end!

entries.title: Acts 3:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Or, Author. Heb. 5.9.

m As God, he is the Author of our Temporal life too, in whom we live, and move, &c. and in whose hand is our breath; but Christ as Mediator, is the guide and way to Eternal life, Iohn 14.6. These are said to have killed our Saviour; tho neither Herod, or Pilate, nor probably many (if any) of them that nailed him to the Cross, were present; but it was done for their sakes, and at their desire, and therefore by their means; and 'tis here charged upon them, as done by them.

Chap. 2.24.

Chap. 2.32.

entries.title: Acts 3:16
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n His power; for by it he is known as men or things are, by their several names; or the Name of Christ is put for Christ himself, as the Name of God is put for God commonly.

o Calling by Faith on the Name of Christ; being thorowly perswaded that he could and would heal this cripple.

p Not onely Faith, as on Christ as its Object: but by and from Christ as its Author: Faith being twice made mention of in this cure, there being required Faith in Peter to heal, and in the lame man to be healed.

entries.title: Acts 3:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q Lest the Corrasive in the 13, 14, 15. verses, should pierce too far, to prevent despair in his Auditors, the Apostle useth in this verse a lenitive calling them; yet, Brethren, tho guilty of so great a mistake in their judgment and fault in their practice.

q Whatsoever they did against Christ, whom St. Peter Preached, was out of a double error. 1. About the place of Christs Birth, supposing him to have been born at Nazareth. 2. They were ignorant of the nature of this Kingdom.

Luke 23.34. 1 Cor. 2.[illegible].

s Whose fault was the greater, as having seduced others, &c. Yet St. Peter opens a door of hope by repentance, even for them also.

entries.title: Acts 3:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
t The Prophets did all speak the same things, as if they had spoken out of one mouth, as they did speak by one Spirit.

u God used the ignorance of some, and the malice of others, for his own holy ends: and that it was Prophesied that Christ should suffer, is very plain. Isaiah 50.5, 6, 7.

entries.title: Acts 3:19
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 2.38.

y Alluding to the manner of writing upon Tables in those times, and not much disagreeing from what is in use amongst us, who write upon paper or parchment; there is a book of remembrance, and a record of all our sins kept, Ier. 17.1. The sin of Iudah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond: when sin is pardoned, it is said to be blotted out, Isa. 44.22. and not to be found any more, tho it should be sought for, Ier 50.20.

z Or times of cooling; as afflictions are called a fiery tryal, so deliverance from them, is a season of refreshing or cooling: Such a time of refreshing shall come in this life, commonly from many troubles; but when this life ends, a deliverance comes from all afflictions to them that truly fear and serve God.

a Gods presence is the cause and ground, from whence all the refreshment his people take, do arise; Heaven would not be Heaven (a place of bliss and glory) without it: and as God is the object of our beatitude, so he is the giver of all comfort, and his Spirit is the onely Comforter.

x This is the true end, use, and application, both of the preceding Miracle and Sermon, to perswade unto Repentance and Conversion.

entries.title: Acts 3:20
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: b To remove all evils and miseries from his people, when that sun shines, all clouds and mists are scattered; this refers especially to Christs second coming, which is here promised to encourage us to do good, and to deter us from doing evil: as also to move us to repentance, and to com [illegible]ort us when penitent.

entries.title: Acts 3:21
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c That is, contain after it hath received him, as a real place doth a true body; for such Christs body was, which was received into Heaven: and Heaven is the Palace and Throne of this King of Kings, and Lord of Lords, where he shall reign until he hath put all his enemies under his feet, 1 Cor. 15.25.

d Or restauration of all things, when all things shall be restored to that condition from which sin put them: for the fall hath maim'd and disordered the whole Universe; and probably, there is not that excellency in any of the Creatures, which there was at first, before man (for whom they were made) by his sin brought death to himself, and as it were a dead colour over all them; this makes the whole Creation groan and travail in pain until now, Rom. 8.22. But the end of the World will be a time of restitution of all things, unto man especially; who shall be then restored unto God, and to a blessed Immortality: for unless this be granted, all their Preaching and Prophesying was in vain, 1 Cor. 15.14.

entries.title: Acts 3:22
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 7.37.

e Their Ancestors in the wilderness, Deut. 18.15. as also in the 8. ver. St. Peter names here but one of their Prophets, but a most remarkable one.

f 1. In Wisdom. 2. In Miracles. 3. In being a Mediator betwixt God and his people. 4. In their being both out of their brethren, (i. e. of the seed of Abraham) 5. In that they were both sent from God after an extraordinary manner.

g If any Prophet did come amongst them, and did foretel future things which came to pass, or did work a real miracle, they were bound to believe him, if he did not endeavour to draw them to worship a false God; and by consequence they were bound to have believed our Saviour, who taught them onely to fear that true God, whom the Law and all the Prophets had spoken of.

entries.title: Acts 3:23
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h That is, every [illegible].

i That is, believe and obey him.

k As those that disobeyed Moses were destroyed, many perishing by strange and sudden deaths, Namb. 16.3. &c. We read of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, and all that belonged to them, swallowed up for this sin. The Apostle demands, Hebr. 2.2. How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation? For a greater than Moses is here, and God hath undertaken to require it of every one that will not hearken unto him, Deut. 18.19.

entries.title: Acts 3:24
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: l Tho there were some Prophets betwixt Moses and Samuel, yet they were but such as Prophesied in some particular exigences and cases; and in Samuels days the word of the Lord was pretious or rare, 1 Samuel 3.1. but then David, that lively Type of Christ, appearing at the Throne, the Messi[illegible]h began to be more discovered in, and by him: Besides, Samuel was the first who wrote his Prophesies, and erected the Schools of the Prophets, and therefore he is first mentioned; and the date of the Prophets is here begun from him.

entries.title: Acts 3:25
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m The Patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob, are called Prophets, Psal. 105.15. and did Prophesie, foretelling things to come, &c. The Disciples of the Prophets are also called their Children or Sons, 2 Kings 2.3. and so these pretended and desired to be accounted.

n Children of the Covenant, are such unto whom the Covenant belong, which God made with Abraham and his seed; hence they are called the children of promise, Rom. 9.8. Gal. 4.28. and the children of the Kingdom, Matth. 8.12. [illegible]nd this Covenant of God with Abraham, was the cause, that notwithstanding all the for[illegible] and heavy calamities of that people, God did always preserve some, and there was a remnant saved.

Gen. 12.3. and 18.18. [illegible] 2[illegible].18. & 26.4.

o Families or Nations.

p Through Christ who is this seed of Abraham, all mercies in this World, and Eternal Life in the World to come are bestowed; grace, and glory, and every good thing.

entries.title: Acts 3:26
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Chap. 13.4[illegible].

q The Iews and Inhabitants of Ierusalem, who are the lost sheep of the house of Israel. St. Peter did not yet know that the Gentiles should be called, until he was taught it by the vision, Acts 10. almost throughout; and tho our Saviour had told the Apostles, that they should be his witnesses to the uttermost parts of the earth, Acts 1.8. they understood it onely of those of their own Nation, scattered or dispersed abroad, 1 Peter 1.1.

r Which word does not onely refer to the Resurrection of Christ, but to his being constituted and appointed to be a Prince and a Saviour; thus 'tis said, a great Prophet is risen up amongst us, Luke 7.16. and God hath raised up a horn of Salvation, Luke 1.69. Howsoever, it is by vertue of Christ[illegible] being raised from the dead, and carried into his Kingdom, that we are blessed.

s This is the greatest blessing indeed; hence our Saviour hath his name imposed by God on him, Matth. 1.21. and was called Jesus, because he saves his people from their sins; and without this being saved from our sins, nothing can be a blessing to us, Isaiah 3.11. and 57.21. There is no peace saith my God to the wicked: add to this, that if any be turned from their iniquities, it is through the blessing of God in Christ.

entries.title: Acts 4:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c Or angry to such a degree, that it was a great trouble to them.

d The Doctrine of the Resurrection alone, could not but vex the Sadduces who denied it: but it did more afflict them, that the Apostles Preached it through Jesus; asserting, not onely the Resurrection of our Saviour, which the Iews gave so much money unto the Soldiers to hinder the report of, Matth. 28.12, 13. but also that Christ was the Author of the Resurrection, and the first fruits of them that sleep; and because they inferred from Christs Resurrection, that his Disciples should rise from the dead also.

entries.title: Acts 4:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: e Some think, this not to have been so strait a custody as that of a prison: but that rather the Apostles were delivered to some, that promised that they should be forth coming; the prediction of our Saviour began now to be fulfilled, Luke 21.12. They shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you. Howsoever, God was pleased to suffer persecution to come by degrees on his Church; after the Sun was down, (Christ was gone from them) it was not presently pitch-darkness with them. God always remembers his peoples condition, and his own promise; and lays no more upon them, than they are able to bear.

entries.title: Acts 4:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Faith cometh by bearing, and hearing by the word of God, Rom. 10.17. It being the ordinary means which God hath appointed; the Apostles themselves make use of it towards the conviction of this people.

g The number of the hearers is not intended to be set here, or in any other place; but either these five thousand, were such as were Converted at this Sermon, or rather the number Converted by St. Peters former Sermon, Chap. 2.14, 41. were at this Sermon made thus many; howsoever the increase which God gave was very great.

entries.title: Acts 4:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h The Sanhedrim or great Council.

i The Magistrates of the City, Scribes, Doctors, or Teachers of the Law, &c howsoever these might be distinguished, they are all as one against the Doctrine of the Gospel, and endeavour to put out the light, as soon as it began to shine, as Herod would have killed Christ in the manger.

entries.title: Acts 4:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
John 11.49.

k Both these are said to be High Priests, Luke 3.2. whether they bare this Office by turn each other year, as some think; or that the Roman Power, put in and out whom they pleased, and in courtesie he that was laid aside, still retained the title during his life, is not very material.

l Thought to be the Son of Annas.

m A man of great repute amongst them, as Iosephus says.

n Their relation many times preferring them to a place in their great Councel or Sanhedrim.

o Or in Ierusalem; either such as were in the City, being called together on such an extraordinary occasion; or else they sent also unto men of greatest note, that lived nigh thereunto.

entries.title: Acts 4:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
p The Sanhedrim or great Council, did sit in a circular form; and the Apostles being to answer for themselves, were placed so as they might better hear, and be heard.

Exod. 2.14. Matth. 21.23. Chap. 7.27.

q Natural, or Supernatural and Divine.

r At whose command, or in whose Authority, they inquire whether they did pretend to be Prophets, or persons extraordinarily sent, &c. Tho the Miracle which they had wrought, shewed sufficiently by whose power it was done; yet of this they were willingly ignorant, and enquire onely that they might find matter out of the Apostles own mouths, for which they might blame or punish them.

entries.title: Acts 4:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s Guiding, and strengthning of him, in what he did speak, by which so mightily Peter differed from himself, that tho formerly he was afraid of a servant, and denied our Saviour, now he is not afraid before the Rulers to confess him.

t See ver. 5. These were especially the great Council, in imitation of the Seventy, which Moses appointed by Gods command to help him in the burden of his Government, Numb. 11.16, 24.

entries.title: Acts 4:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u Juridi[illegible]ally called in question; 'tis a forensical word of the good deed; tho they disputed not the Authority of the Court, yet they assert their integrity; that it was no other than a good deed they had done, which Rulers ought not to be a terror unto, Rom. 13.3.

x That is, in the words of the question which was propounded unto them, ver. 7. By what Power, or by what Name he is made whole?

entries.title: Acts 4:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y The Apostles are not dismayed, but make their boldness spoken of, ver. 13. to appear; they Preach Christ to all of them, and wish they could make him known to all others.

z See Chap. 2.22. i. e.

a God the Father: our Surety was discharged by God himself, who had laid him in the prison of the grave for our debts. This

b the lame man that was made whole being present, and an ocular demonstration of the Miracle wrought upon him.

entries.title: Acts 4:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c Alluding to the Psal. 118.22. in which there is a Prophecy of what was now fulfilled, see Chap. 2.23.

d So by their Office they were, and ought to have been so indeed, and are here so called, that they might be minded of their duty, viz. to increase, strengthen, and beautifie the building, and not to demolish, weaken or deface it.

e Or the corner stone; Christ is frequently so called, Matth. 21.42. Mark 12.10. and that, 1. Because he sustains and upholds the whole building. 2. He is a Rock or stone of offence, Rom. 9.33. as many run upon, and are hurt by a corner-stone. 3. He is most precious, 1 Peter 2.6. as the corner-stones are usually the largest, firmest, and best. 4. Christ is a light to lighten the Gentiles, as well as the glory of the people of Israel; and both Gentile and Iew are united in him, and saved by him, as the corner-stone is equally necessary for both sides, which are united in it, and born up by it.

entries.title: Acts 4:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Mat. 1.21. Chap. 10.43. 1 Tim. 2.5, 6.

f For Soul or Body.

g Person or thing.

h Because in distress men did usually call upon their many false gods by name, as O Baal hear us, 1 Kings 18.26.

i Whether Patriarch or Prophet, Priest or King; especially referring unto Moses, in whom they did trust, and therefore under the Gospel especially, we must lift up our hearts.

entries.title: Acts 4:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Not wholly unlearned, but such as were without any polite Learning, or more than ordinary Education, such as every one amongst them had.

l Idiots, so the Greek word from whence ours come, signifying such as was brought up at home, and never acted in a larger sphere, than the walls of their own house; having never been Magistrates, or Teachers of the Law, or any way publick persons; and spake onely their mother Tongue.

m Which these Rulers might easily take notice of; many of them frequenting his company too, Matth. 21.23. Luke 18.8. Iohn 12.42.

entries.title: Acts 4:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n Whereas, before he was either carryed, or was forced to lay down.

o They could not deny but that it was a good deed, and that it was miraculously done.

entries.title: Acts 4:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
p The place where the Council met; for the Apostles were not dismissed to go away at their liberty.

q It was their joynt indeavour to stifle the Gospel, and would now consult about the best expedient, but they would not let the Apostles hear, lest they might discover the weakness of their proofs against them, and against the truth.

entries.title: Acts 4:16
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
John 11.47.

r At what a loss are these great men, about the manner of their proceeding with the Apostles! they might seem to have the victory in their hands, and yet they are evidently overcome by three witnesses, viz. by both the Apostles and the lame man, and especially by the evidence of this fact its self; tho they did not boggle at being unjust, yet they were loath to seem to be so, and therefore they take Counsel to hide it, or palliate it before men; more valuing their credit, than the Salvation of their own, or other mens Souls.

entries.title: Acts 4:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s The Pleonasin here used implies a very sore and heavy threatning; as of the grievousest punishment upon the most heinous fact.

t Either 1. by Preaching, or 2. by praying in it, or 3. by doing Miracles again by it.

entries.title: Acts 4:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x As his Apostles and Ministers sent from him.

n Neither privately nor publickly.

entries.title: Acts 4:19
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y Both spake by one and the same Spirit, and agreed in one and the same answer; they are not sollicitous what will best bring them off at present, but

z from whom nothing is hid, and who is the avenger of all wrong. The Apostles seem to refer to a commonly received rule amongst their Rabbins, which also they make use of, Chap. 5.29. We ought to obey God rather than men.

a In the greatest matters of our most holy Religion, God hath not left himself without a witness, or a thousand witnesses in our own breasts and consciences, Amos 2.11.

entries.title: Acts 4:20
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: b In a moral, not in a Physical sense: they could not refrain speaking, because of the necessity which was laid upon them, and the woe which would have befall'n them, if they had not Preached the Gospel, 1 Cor. 9.16. If any man denies to bear testimony for man to a truth, he sins; how much more does he sin, who forbears to witness for God, and at the command, or the sending of God?

entries.title: Acts 4:21
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c For the present; for amongst them no acquittal was so peremptory or absolute, but that they might be tryed again for the same fact upon further evidence.

Mat. 21.26. Luke 20.6, 19. and 22.2. Chap. 5.26.

d It was not the sense of the evil, or sin, nor the apprehension of Gods displeasure and wrath which deterred them; but the fear or favour of the people. The corruptions that are in the world, are over-ruled for the good of Gods children in it;

e not onely such as believed, but others also could not but confess, that this was the hand of God, which had made the lame to walk, and rejoice in it, and by consequence have a very great veneration for the Apostles, who were the instruments of it.

Chap. 3.7, 8.

entries.title: Acts 4:22
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: f 1. Therefore the harder to be cured. 2. The man was the more credible, who had so long known what it was to be without the use of his limbs, which now he injoyed. 3. Whom they could not themselves but have often seen, and heard begging. But if he had laid so many years in the porch of the Temple through which our Saviour frequently entred, how came it to pass that he was not cured before? We do not read that our Saviour denied any who came for cure. There need no other answer, but that all times and seasons are in Gods hands, who justly forbore to send deliverance till this very time, and now mercifully sent it; especially, reserving this Miracle for the confirmation of the truth of the Gospel, and of the Apostles themselves in the Preaching of it.

entries.title: Acts 4:23
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
g They went to their own company; the rest of the Apostles and believers, who have a special propriety and delight in one another, sheep with sheep, and goats with goats; tho the separation will be made at the last day, the foundation of it is laid here.

Chap. 12.12.

h To forewarn them of what they might expect, and encourage them to hope for the like deliverance

i What hath been said concerning them, might be added, that these it may be were the first or chief in the courses, which David divided the Priests unto, which division was observed till our Saviours time, Luke 1.5.

entries.title: Acts 4:24
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Their own company, believers, unto whom they went.

l Either jointly with one heart and Spirit agreeing in the same words, or saying Amen to the same thing.
